belief: I must never let anyone see me struggle.
origins: In families, workplaces, and communities where success is a sign of status, struggle can feel like exposure. A parent who always looked fine, a culture of “keeping up appearances,” or a past experience when vulnerability was used against us can teach us to hide. The cost is quiet: stress, secrecy, and loneliness among people who think everything is fine.
teaches: Paul wrote that Christ told him, “My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is perfected in weakness.” We are told to bear one another’s burdens, to confess to one another and pray for one another, and to approach the throne of grace with confidence to find help in time of need. God never asked us to look strong. He invites us to bring our weakness to Him and to safe people, because help flows toward honesty.
self_statements: If they knew I was struggling, they would lose respect for me.
I have to look like I have it all together.
Needing help means I have failed.
I cannot afford to be seen as weak.
errors: Predicting that others will judge me if they see my struggle.
Insisting that I must always appear strong.
Seeing myself as either fine or a failure.
Assuming I know what others would think of my struggle.
questions: What have I been hiding, and what has hiding cost me?
Who has been honest with me about their struggles, and what did I think of them?
What do I believe would happen if one safe person knew?
What does God say about weakness?
Where did I learn that struggle must be hidden?
Who is one safe person I could tell?
truth: Everyone struggles, and hiding it does not make me stronger. God’s grace meets me in my weakness, and He gives me people to help carry what I cannot carry alone. I can choose a safe person and let myself be known.
hw_truths: I do not have to look strong to be loved.
God’s power shows up in my weakness.
Asking for help is wise, not weak.
Safe people can carry part of my load.
I can let myself be known.
log: Each week, note one honest thing you shared with a safe person, and what happened afterward.
actions: Choose someone who is trustworthy, discreet, and kind.
Tell that person one honest thing and notice how they respond.
Tell God exactly where you are struggling, without polish.
If the struggle involves money, health, or family, contact a counselor, advisor, or pastor this week.
prayer: Father, You see my struggle and You are not ashamed of me. Give me courage to be honest with You and with safe people. Let Your power be made perfect in my weakness. Amen.
hw_questions: Who is a safe person I could tell?
What does God say about weakness?
What is one honest step I can take?
Where did I learn to hide struggle?
name_example: Sarah can write: “God’s grace is enough for me, even when I am weak, so I can let a safe person help.”
